questions.q: What is the very first prerequisite step before installing SQL Server as an FCI, per this lesson?
options: Building a working Windows Server Failover Cluster (WSFC) with the Failover Clustering feature enabled
Installing SQL Server as a standalone instance first
Creating the Availability Group listener
Configuring log shipping between the nodes
questions.explain: An FCI cannot exist without a working WSFC underneath it — this is a hard prerequisite the SQL Server installer checks for.

questions.q: What must happen to shared storage before running SQL Server Setup for an FCI?
options: It must be presented to the cluster and added as cluster shared storage, validated ahead of time
Nothing — the SQL Server installer configures shared storage automatically
It should be split into separate, unshared disks per node
It only needs to be configured after SQL Server is already installed
questions.explain: Shared storage has to be configured and validated as cluster shared storage before the installer is run, because Setup expects it to already exist.

questions.q: Which SQL Server Setup option is used on the very first node to create a new FCI?
options: New SQL Server Failover Cluster Installation
Add node to a SQL Server failover cluster
Standalone Installation
Upgrade an existing instance
questions.explain: The first node uses 'New SQL Server Failover Cluster Installation' to create the instance, its VNN, and data/log paths.

questions.q: What does 'Add node to a SQL Server failover cluster' actually do, per this lesson?
options: Makes an additional cluster node able to host the already-created FCI during a future failover
Creates a brand-new, separate SQL Server instance on that node
Adds a new database to the existing instance
Configures log shipping to that node
questions.explain: It doesn't create a new instance — it enables that node to take over hosting the existing FCI when a failover happens.

questions.q: An administrator tries 'New SQL Server Failover Cluster Installation' on a server that isn't part of any WSFC cluster yet. What happens?
options: Setup won't offer that installation path at all — a validated WSFC cluster has to exist first
SQL Server automatically creates the WSFC cluster on the fly
The installation proceeds normally with reduced functionality
SQL Server installs as an Availability Group replica instead
questions.explain: The failover cluster installation path explicitly depends on an existing, validated WSFC cluster — it isn't something Setup creates for you.
